entries.contract: `forget` withdraws a fact from active recall (src/core/facts/forget.ts header; docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md); context_pack is a memory verb that packs hot facts; the hot-memory cache says it is "Refreshed on extraction event via bumpCache" (src/core/facts/meta-hook.ts:10).

entries.actual: Both still carry it for up to 30 s in a running stdio or HTTP server. N5 counted run: 2 prohibited context_pack outputs on the PGLite cells and 12 on Postgres; 108 PGLite and 304 Postgres remote responses carried a forgotten canary in _meta after its forget returned.

entries.contract: forget withdraws only the forgotten claim; other facts on the page stay readable (src/core/facts/withdrawal.ts). A refused write is not applied: owner_unavailable is a retryable refusal (src/core/connectors/item-holds.ts:97).

entries.actual: The page keeps 0 chunks and its retained facts are missing from search, query and the recall query arm until an unrelated later write drains the queue (repro: 2 of 5 rounds, with forget returning ok). In the N5 PGLite CLI cell both late forgets answered owner_unavailable although they had committed, and 4 retained neighbors (12 of 750 retained pairs) went missing from the chunk tiers.

entries.contract: docs/guides/open-loops.md: "last substantive message is theirs, you're in To:, unanswered >=24h -> unanswered_inbound"; src/core/google/loop-detect.ts close-lane comment: a fresh counterparty nudge inside the grace window is not a reply and must not hide the loop "exactly while the counterparty was most impatient".

entries.actual: No loop: the grace window is measured from the nudge, so 6 of 6 such threads (and 4 of 4 outbound follow-ups) are invisible on first sync (backfill or after a sync gap) until the nudge itself ages past the window. Steady-state syncs that saw the request first keep the loop open (hold).

entries.contract: docs/guides/open-loops.md: "a reply lands -> the loop closes itself (closed_by: reply_detected)"; close semantics: "Thread loops close deterministically when a reply lands." Any reply is documented to close; acknowledgements are not distinguished.

entries.actual: The acknowledgement closes the reply-owed loop as documented (4 of 4 store rounds closed by reply_detected); 13 of 23 threads closed by my reply are still owed by the semantic labels.

entries.contract: docs/guides/open-loops.md close semantics: "Fulfillment-by-reply detection for commitments is future work, not pretended at." src/core/google/loops-extract.ts persistence upserts extracted commitments only.
entries.surface: src/core/google/loops-extract.ts runLoopsExtract; src/core/loops/loops-store.ts upsertOpenLoop
entries.expected: A commitment loop closes when a later message in the thread fulfils it ("As promised, here is the deck").
entries.actual: Nothing marks a stored commitment fulfilled: re-extraction can only upsert what the model returns, the reply auto-close touches deterministic_thread loops only, and staleness closes llm_extract loops by age. Keyless the extractor refuses (llm_unavailable). The preregistered paid replay (docs/benchmarks/2026-10-01-n7-open-loops-email/receipt-extractor-pin.json) saw the model correctly omit all 4 fulfilled promises on a single pass, yet all 4 commitment loops extracted before the fulfilling message stayed open after it was extracted.

entries.contract: None broken: src/core/entities/resolve.ts:13-21 and :32-34 document that a bare one-word name resolves only when prefix expansion finds exactly one candidate; collisions fall through.
entries.surface: src/core/entities/resolve.ts:280-283 resolveEntitySlugWithSource (bare-name prefix expansion)
entries.repro: bun eval/runner/n9-multi-hop-paraphrase.ts (data.one_hop.per_query: parsed true, seeds_resolved 0, templates works_at, invested_in, advises)
entries.expected: as a capability: "Who works at Acme?" resolves Acme to companies/acme-0, whose title is exactly "Acme"
entries.actual: "Acme" collides with companies/acme-labs-50 under prefix expansion, falls back to slugify and the arm does not fire. 15 of 145 world-v1 one-hop template questions are affected (8 works_at, 5 invested_in, 2 advises: Acme, Delta, Epsilon, Helix, Iris, Nimbus, Quantum, Vector)
entries.reason: documented precision-first resolver design, not a broken contract; an exact-title tier for bare names would be a product change

entries.contract: parseConversation must not flip prose with a few stray anchors to regex_match, because that "silently corrupts downstream fact extraction" (src/core/conversation-parser/parse.ts SCORING_MIN_ACCEPTANCE comment); bold-name-no-time sets score_full_body so "a notes page with a few bold labels" is no_match (src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts).
entries.surface: src/core/conversation-parser/parse.ts parseConversation (bold-name-no-time, score_full_body)
entries.expected: A 26-line status note with three one-off labels (**Status:**, **Owner:**, **Next step:**) parses as no_match with 0 messages.
entries.actual: regex_match via bold-name-no-time with 3 messages whose speakers are Status, Owner and Next step. The full-body density guard only helps long pages (3 of 26 non-blank lines is above the 5% floor); every label occurs once, which a real transcript almost never does.

entries.contract: TranscriptMessage.timestamp is "ISO 8601 UTC, from the SOURCE" (src/core/transcripts/types.ts) and rendered pages carry REAL timestamps (src/core/transcripts/render.ts header).
entries.surface: src/core/transcripts/render.ts anchorTimestamp (day from iso.slice(0, 10), hour from getUTCHours); codex, openclaw, claude-code and claude-export adapters pass source timestamp strings through unconverted
entries.actual: The adapter keeps the -07:00 string, the anchor reads (2026-08-10 5:30 AM) and the re-parsed turn is 2026-08-10T05:30:00Z, one day early (16 of 16 offset-stamped turns across the four ISO-string adapters). buildTranscriptSlug takes its date from the same local slice. Every host fixture in gbrain writes Z, so only sources that write offsets are affected.

entries.contract: transcriptAdapters() is the one registry of import formats (src/core/transcripts/detect.ts); the capability matrix (N12, P8) lists no generic JSON adapter.
entries.surface: src/core/transcripts/detect.ts transcriptAdapters; src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts
entries.expected: A generic {messages:[{role, content, timestamp}]} transcript imports (if gbrain claimed it).
entries.actual: detectAdapter reports unknown_format and parseConversation returns no_match for a JSON body.
entries.reason: Not claimed at this commit; recorded as a coverage gap, not a failure (wave amendment 3).

entries.contract: MatchedMessage.timestamp "may be 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z for time-only formats when no frontmatter date is available" (src/core/conversation-parser/types.ts).
entries.surface: src/core/conversation-parser/parse.ts deriveDateContext
entries.expected: A date for time-only and no-time patterns when the page has none.
entries.actual: 1970-01-01 on 494 of 494 date-less turns parsed with no page date (13 time-only and no-time patterns x 38 turns); inline-date patterns keep their dates.
entries.reason: Documented fallback; the page date in frontmatter is the supported path, and with it every timed turn matched at minute precision.

entries.contract: Built-in patterns capture hours and minutes only (CaptureMap has no seconds group, src/core/conversation-parser/types.ts).
entries.surface: src/core/conversation-parser/builtins.ts (bold-paren-time, telegram-text-export, whatsapp-iso, signal-export)
entries.expected: Seconds written in the line survive (if claimed).
entries.actual: Seconds dropped on 36 of 152 turns rendered in the four formats whose lines carry seconds (seed 12).
entries.reason: Minute precision by design; recorded so a reader does not read minute-exact as source-exact.

entries.contract: Attendance evidence is a ## Attendees link list, an Attendees: or **Attendees:** line, or frontmatter attendees (src/core/link-extraction.ts attendanceEvidenceRanges, FRONTMATTER_LINK_MAP); attendance is not a parser output (capability matrix N12).
entries.surface: src/core/link-extraction.ts extractPageLinks (meeting pages)
entries.expected: People listed on a Participants: line, or who only speak in a transcript, are typed attended (if claimed).
entries.actual: 0 of 10 such attendees typed attended (participants-line 0 of 5, speakers-only 0 of 5); they stay mentions or carry no link.
entries.reason: Not a documented evidence form; documented forms score 20 of 20 with zero false attendance.

entries.contract: The bundled legacy gbrain-base pack declares attended with inference.page_type: meeting, and a pack-declared verb wins over the in-code attendance-evidence check (src/core/schema-pack/base/gbrain-base.yaml; src/core/link-extraction.ts typeFor). gbrain init writes gbrain-base-v2 (src/commands/init.ts).
entries.surface: src/core/link-extraction.ts extractPageLinks with the gbrain-base pack (schema_pack unset)
entries.expected: A person only mentioned in a meeting page's notes is typed mentions.
entries.actual: With schema_pack unset, every linked person is typed attended: 24 of 24 mentioned-only people across 12 meetings. With gbrain-base-v2, 0 of 24.
entries.reason: Behaviour declared by the legacy pack, not a broken contract: evidence-gated attendance exists only under gbrain-base-v2. Brains with no schema_pack configured (created before init wrote one) still get it; a fix would apply the evidence gate to pack-declared attended too, or migrate such brains to v2.

entries.contract: A category measures the configuration a default install runs (wave plan section 3; gbrain init writes schema_pack gbrain-base-v2).
entries.surface: eval/runner/n12-format-fidelity.ts attendanceStage

entries.expected: The attendance stage configures schema_pack as gbrain init does.
entries.actual: The first development run left schema_pack unset, so it measured the legacy pack (24 false attendances). Fixed in gbrain-evals before the counted run; the unset arm is kept as an exploratory row.
entries.reason: Harness defect in gbrain-evals, corrected before any counted number; see N12-7 for the gbrain-side behaviour it exposed.

entries.contract: "A symbol type code-def can resolve must never have its symbol_name erased by small-sibling merging" (src/core/chunkers/def-types.ts header, #4511); code-def resolves lexical declarations (DEF_TYPES).
entries.surface: src/core/chunkers/code.ts mergeSmallSiblings; src/core/chunkers/def-types.ts MERGEABLE_RUN_TYPES (lexical declaration stays mergeable)
entries.expected: code_def int2alpha returns src/sample.ts:3 (a nine-line `const int2alpha = (...) => {...}`).
entries.actual: code_def returns 0 results; lines 1-16 are one anonymous merged chunk. On pathe, 9 of 50 top-level functions (all `const` arrow functions in src/_glob.ts) are unreachable, and 3 same-file calls they make lose their caller name.

entries.contract: code_callers returns callers with a resolved flag, documented with resolved: true for a resolved edge (src/core/operations-descriptions.ts CODE_CALLERS_DESCRIPTION).

entries.actual: resolved: false with edge_metadata.resolved_chunk_id set. On pathe, resolved is false on 81 of 81 caller edges while 53 carry resolved_chunk_id.

entries.contract: code_blast and code_flow support TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript and Python (src/core/code-intel/recursive-walk.ts SUPPORTED_LANGS).

entries.contract: code_refs is a substring ILIKE over chunk text (src/commands/code-refs.ts header; capability matrix N13).
entries.surface: code_refs
entries.expected: Semantic references only (if claimed).
entries.actual: 130 of 291 returned chunks across 50 symbols hold only a substring (for example join inside .join() calls), while 167 of 171 compiler references are covered.
entries.reason: Documented: lexical references are not semantic references.

entries.contract: The symbol resolver resolves within one file only (src/core/chunkers/symbol-resolver.ts header).

entries.actual: 0 of 12 cross-file calls resolved; all 12 appear in code_callers only through a bare-name match, which also matches same-named functions in other files (pathe has two parse functions).
entries.reason: Documented limit of the resolver.

entries.reason: Not claimed at this commit.

entries.contract: The edge extractor emits a bare callee token when it cannot type a receiver (obj.m() becomes m), and the within-file resolver resolves a token that matches exactly one same-file qualified name (src/core/chunkers/edge-extractor.ts and symbol-resolver.ts headers).
entries.surface: resolve_symbol_edges cycle phase (src/core/chunkers/symbol-resolver.ts)
entries.expected: A member call such as segments.join("/") or process.cwd() is not resolved to a same-named top-level function.
entries.actual: On pathe, dirname, relative and format are resolved callers of pathe's join (they call Array.prototype.join), and cwd is a resolved caller of itself (it calls process.cwd()): 4 of 53 resolved edges.
entries.reason: Consequence of the documented bare-token emission for untyped receivers; precision cost of within-file resolution, not a broken contract. Worth a receiver-aware guard before blast radius is trusted.
